apps.name: PhotoSwiper
apps.subtitle: Swipe your camera roll
apps.localizedDescription: Tinder-style photo curation. Swipe left = delete, right = save to Immich, up = share to the other person via Messages.
apps.versionDescription: Phase 3.1: trash-bucket delete model. Left swipe now queues photos for delete instead of deleting one at a time. New trash badge in the toolbar shows the pending count — tap it to delete the whole batch with ONE iOS confirmation. Undo actually keeps photos in your library now. Pending bucket survives app quit.

versions.localizedDescription: Phase 3.1: trash-bucket delete model. Left swipe queues photos for batch delete (no more tap-to-confirm per photo). Toolbar trash badge shows the pending count; tap it to commit (one iOS confirmation for the whole batch) or discard. Undo really works now — photos never leave your library until you confirm the batch. Pending bucket persists across app quits.

Phase 3: swipe actions wired. Left = delete from device (iOS confirms first). Up = share via the system share sheet (Messages, Mail, AirDrop). Down = skip ('I'll get to it later'). Right = placeholder log (real Immich upload lands in Phase 4). New undo button in the top-left toolbar reverses the most recent swipe.
Phase 2.1: photo browsing + first-launch permission prompt. Swipe through your camera roll in random or oldest-first order. Swipe actions are placeholders (no delete/upload/share yet — Phase 3).

privacy.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: PhotoSwiper needs access to show and curate your photos.
privacy.NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription: Save photos back to your library after editing.
